To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the earth has a limited capacity to absorb the wastes and pollution produced by modern industrial civilization, and that this capacity has already been seriously exceeded in many parts of the world.
man is part of the natural world and that the natural world is part of man.
the world is a single, finite system, in which the resources of the earth are finite and not replaceable, and the earth is a living system, in which all parts are interdependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: the development of the human species and the development of the earth; the relationship between science technology industry and economy; the development of the natural environment and the development of human living arrangements; and the strategies for survival.
the relationship between human beings and their natural environment.
the interdependence of man and nature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the world has been in a state of ecological imbalance for a long time and that it will take many years to correct this imbalance.
man must change his ways.
the earth is not only a small planet, but also a fragile planet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are in the midst of a transition from a society based on the exploitation of nature to one based on the management of natural resources.
we must develop the capacity to understand and to control the processes which determine the quality of our environment and the quality of our own life.

man has to live on earth in a way which is not only compatible with the survival of the earth as a living organism but which also makes possible the full realization of his human capacities and aspirations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we must change our ways of thinking about the earth and the way we live on it.
the world has a problem and it is a big one.
the earth is one and interrelated and the human race must be prepared to act as one.
